items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: and Fletcher got these particular guys to augment his band

ctx.x: Well, he was an excellent player. He's an official in the union there in Los Angeles now. But he was a great trumpet player, and Fletcher got these particular guys to augment his band, and I think he played the Plantation for three weeks, or something like that, then he started back East. And this is when I decided to stay in California, and this is when I joined Lena Horne as her pianist and arranger, and we made a tour. We started our tour -- we first went to

San Francisco, played (unintelligible): the theaters and all. Fletcher said, "Do you mean you're not going back East?" I says, "No." I like California. I like this, and I'm gonna stay." I had no idea what I was gonna do. I was just gonna take a chance. I liked it. And I happened to have been staying at a place in California with a guy that's got quite a name, and he played with a name band and that was Juan Tizol, the great trombonist --
